"""Tests for first-run onboarding signal extraction and gating."""

from __future__ import annotations

from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
from agentic_odi_cli import onboard, profile


class _Response:
    def __init__(self, text: str, url: str = "https://acme.test/product") -> None:
        self.text = text
        self.url = url

    def raise_for_status(self) -> None:
        return None


def test_page_signals_repr_summarises_the_fetch() -> None:
    signals = onboard.PageSignals(
        title="Acme",
        meta_description="desc",
        domain="acme.test",
        primary_user=None,
        business_model=None,
        core_problem=None,
        current_focus=None,
        confidence="high",
    )

    assert signals.title == "Acme"
    assert "Acme" in repr(signals)
    assert "acme.test" in repr(signals)


def test_infer_baseline_marks_keyword_rich_pages_high_confidence() -> None:
    signals = onboard.PageSignals(
        title="DevTools error tracking and monitoring",
        meta_description="performance analytics",
        domain="acme.test",
        primary_user="engineers",
        business_model="saas",
        core_problem="debugging",
        current_focus="launch",
        confidence=None,
    )

    baseline, scores = onboard.infer_baseline(signals)

    assert baseline.source == "url"
    assert baseline.domain == "acme.test"
    assert baseline.primary_user == "engineers"
    assert baseline.confidence == "high"
    assert scores["devtools"] == 3
    assert scores["error"] == 2


def test_infer_baseline_marks_keyword_poor_pages_low_confidence() -> None:
    signals = onboard.PageSignals(
        title="Acme",
        meta_description="A friendly product",
        domain=None,
        primary_user=None,
        business_model=None,
        core_problem=None,
        current_focus=None,
        confidence=None,
    )

    baseline, scores = onboard.infer_baseline(signals)

    assert baseline.domain == ""
    assert baseline.confidence == "low"
    assert scores == {}


def test_extract_signals_reads_title_meta_and_domain() -> None:
    html = (
        "<html><head><title>Acme DevTools</title>"
        '<meta name="description" content="Error tracking for teams">'
        "</head></html>"
    )

    signals = onboard._extract_signals(html, "https://acme.test/product")

    assert signals.title == "Acme DevTools"
    assert signals.meta_description == "Error tracking for teams"
    assert signals.domain == "acme.test"
    assert signals.confidence == "high"


def test_extract_signals_defaults_missing_metadata_to_empty() -> None:
    signals = onboard._extract_signals("<html></html>", "https://acme.test")

    assert signals.title == ""
    assert signals.meta_description == ""
    assert signals.confidence == "low"


def test_fetch_signals_returns_a_baseline_for_reachable_pages(monkeypatch) -> None:
    html = "<html><head><title>DevTools error tracking</title></head></html>"
    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.httpx, "get", lambda *args, **kwargs: _Response(html))

    baseline, low_confidence = onboard.fetch_signals("https://acme.test")

    assert baseline.domain == "acme.test"
    assert baseline.confidence == "high"
    assert low_confidence is False


def test_fetch_signals_falls_back_to_typed_path_on_fetch_errors(monkeypatch) -> None:
    def _boom(*args, **kwargs):
        raise RuntimeError("offline")

    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.httpx, "get", _boom)

    signals, low_confidence = onboard.fetch_signals("https://acme.test")

    assert isinstance(signals, onboard.PageSignals)
    assert signals.title == ""
    assert signals.confidence == "low"
    assert low_confidence is True


def test_fetch_signals_falls_back_when_the_status_is_an_error(monkeypatch) -> None:
    class _ErrorResponse(_Response):
        def raise_for_status(self) -> None:
            raise RuntimeError("500")

    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.httpx, "get", lambda *args, **kwargs: _ErrorResponse("ignored"))

    signals, low_confidence = onboard.fetch_signals("https://acme.test")

    assert isinstance(signals, onboard.PageSignals)
    assert signals.title == ""
    assert low_confidence is True


def test_contract_copy_is_available() -> None:
    assert any("consent" in line for line in onboard.HONESTY_CONTRACT_LINES)
    assert any("Product" in line for line in onboard.CARD_LINES)


def _interactive(monkeypatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.sys, "stdin", SimpleNamespace(isatty=lambda: True))
    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.sys, "stdout", SimpleNamespace(isatty=lambda: True))


def test_maybe_run_first_launch_skips_when_no_onboard(monkeypatch, capsys) -> None:
    _interactive(monkeypatch)

    onboard.maybe_run_first_launch(no_onboard=True)

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""


def test_maybe_run_first_launch_skips_when_a_baseline_exists(monkeypatch, capsys) -> None:
    _interactive(monkeypatch)
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile, "baseline_exists", lambda: True)

    onboard.maybe_run_first_launch()

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""


def test_maybe_run_first_launch_skips_without_a_tty(monkeypatch, capsys) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.sys, "stdin", SimpleNamespace(isatty=lambda: False))
    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.sys, "stdout", SimpleNamespace(isatty=lambda: True))
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile, "baseline_exists", lambda: False)

    onboard.maybe_run_first_launch()

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""


@pytest.mark.parametrize("subcommand", ["setup", "profile", "version", "help"])
def test_maybe_run_first_launch_skips_management_subcommands(
    monkeypatch, capsys, subcommand
) -> None:
    _interactive(monkeypatch)
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile, "baseline_exists", lambda: False)

    onboard.maybe_run_first_launch(invoked_subcommand=subcommand)

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""


def test_maybe_run_first_launch_shows_the_card(monkeypatch) -> None:
    _interactive(monkeypatch)
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile, "baseline_exists", lambda: False)
    printed: list[str] = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.typer, "echo", printed.append)

    onboard.maybe_run_first_launch()

    output = "".join(printed)
    assert "First-run onboarding card" in output
    assert "consent" in output

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class EvidenceDraft(BaseModel):

def drafts_from_batch(
    batch: IngestBatch,
    *,
    job_id: str | None = None,
    step_id: str | None = None,
    outcome_id: str | None = None,
    include_catalog: bool = False,
) -> list[EvidenceDraft]:
    """Turn every evidence-bearing record in ``batch`` into a draft.

# Repository Architecture

Agentic ODI is a uv workspace with a single root `pyproject.toml` for shared tooling. Python distributions are imported by their stable `agentic_odi_*` package names; directory layout does not leak into imports.

## Layout

```text
apps/
  cli/            agentic_odi_cli         Typer CLI: local SQLite or remote MCP
  mcp-server/     agentic_odi_mcp_server  FastMCP server over HTTP
  studio-api/     agentic_odi_studio_api  FastAPI sidecar for the Studio SPA
  studio/         React + TypeScript + Vite SPA and Tauri 2 shell
packages/
  core/           agentic_odi_core        Domain, services, repositories, contract
  connectors/     agentic_odi_connectors  MCP client connectors and catalog
infra/cloudflare/ Worker script; wrangler.jsonc lives at the repo root
scripts/          Dev launcher, binary build, installer checks
tests/            Cross-package contract and launcher tests only
docs/             Architecture, reference material, Superpowers artifacts
packaging/        PyInstaller spec for the CLI binary
```

## Dependency Direction

```text
apps/cli ──────────────┐
apps/mcp-server ───────┼──▶ packages/core
apps/studio-api ───────┘         ▲
                                 │
apps/cli ──────────────▶ packages/connectors
```

- `packages/core` depends on no other workspace package.
- `packages/connectors` depends on `core` only where it needs shared models.
- Every runnable app may depend on `core`; none of them imports another app.
- The React SPA only talks to `apps/studio-api` over `/api`; it never calls MCP or the LLM directly.

## Persistence

- `SQLiteRepository` is the production default for the CLI, MCP server, and Studio API.
- The default database is `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_DB`.
- Studio conversation history and PM memory use a separate SQLite database,
  `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`. They are
  sidecar-local and never enter the ODI repository or the MCP contract.
- `build_repository()` chooses SQLite by default and `InMemoryRepository` when `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:`, which is what tests use.
- The CLI selects its backend with `--backend local|mcp` or `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND`.
- The Studio API selects `local` (direct service calls) or `mcp` (passthrough) with `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` or `create_app(backend=...)`.

## MCP Contract

`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` owns `ToolName`, `ToolSpec`, `TOOL_SPECS`, and `TOOL_NAMES`. The live FastMCP registry is asserted against it by `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py`; the CLI's local handlers are checked by `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py`.

## Entry Points

| Command | Module |
|---|---|
| `agentic-odi` | `agentic_odi_cli.cli:app` |
| `agentic-odi-server` / `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | `agentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server:main` |
| `agentic-odi-studio-api` | `agentic_odi_studio_api.main:main` |
| `uv run python scripts/dev.py` | Dev launcher (MCP + Studio API) |

## Related

- [Data flow](data-flow.md)
- [Testing](testing.md)

1: # Development
2: 
3: Everything below mirrors what CI runs. Install the workspace first:
4: 
5: ```bash
6: uv sync --all-packages
7: ```
8: 
9: ## Linting, Formatting & Type Checks
10: 
11: Shared tooling lives in the root `pyproject.toml`, so one command covers every
12: Python project:
13: 
14: ```bash
15: uv run ruff check .
16: uv run ruff format --check .
17: uv run mypy apps brand packages
18: uv run --directory website mypy .
19: 
20: # Security scanning
21: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages website/
22: ```
23: 
24: ## Frontend & Desktop Checks (studio)
25: 
26: The SPA and Tauri shell mirror their CI jobs locally:
27: 
28: ```bash
29: npm --prefix apps/studio run lint       # ESLint
30: npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
31: npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run  # Vitest (run once)
32: npm --prefix apps/studio run build      # production build → apps/studio/dist
33: cd apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check
34: ```
35: 
36: ### Conversational UI coverage
37: 
38: The agent-composed surfaces and the first-run tour are covered at these levels:
39: 
40: | File | What it covers |
41: |---|---|
42: | `apps/studio/src/ui/protocol.test.ts` | Spec parsing: prop types, enums, ranges, required props, depth/node/size ceilings, unknown types |
43: | `apps/studio/src/ui/UiRenderer.test.tsx` | Card rendering, computed opportunity scores, action dispatch, per-node failure isolation, catalog/registry parity |
44: | `apps/studio/src/components/chat/Conversation.test.tsx` | Prose and surfaces interleaved in the agent's order; card actions become messages |
45: | `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_ui_spec.py` | Catalog validation and `render_ui` tool-schema generation |
46: | `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_chat_ui.py` | `render_ui` interception, `ui` SSE events, and the correction fed back to the model |
47: | `apps/studio/src/features/flags.test.ts` | Flag precedence (query → storage → env → default), value parsing, local overrides |
48: | `apps/studio/src/onboarding/machine.test.ts` | Tour transitions, no forward motion without a goal, versioned storage, malformed records |
49: | `apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.test.tsx` | Auto-open, full flow to a destination, skip/Escape, focus trap, resume, replay, inline model repair, flag off |
50: | `apps/studio/src/App.test.tsx` | First-run ordering: tour over the context conversation, job handoff, chosen surface opens, flag off in shell tests |
51: 
52: ## Website Checks (GitHub Pages)
53: 
54: The `website/` static site is part of the main CI workflow. Its tests assert the
55: committed OG art is reproducible, that `index.html` stays in sync with the
56: README, and that the publish pipeline (`website/tests/test_pages_deploy.py`)
57: still exists:
58: 
59: ```bash
60: uv run --directory website pytest tests/
61: ```
62: 
63: Publishing happens in `.github/workflows/pages.yml`: it runs those tests, builds
64: `_site` from `website/`, and deploys the artifact with `actions/deploy-pages` on
65: every push to `main`. There is no `gh-pages` branch, so that workflow is the only
66: thing that keeps <https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/> online.
67: 
68: ## Formatting workflow
69: 
70: - **When editing Python files**, either rely on the **pre-commit hooks** below
71:   (recommended) or run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:
72: 
73:   ```bash
74:   uv run ruff format .
75:   ```
76: 
77: - **CI behavior**:
78:   - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files.
79:   - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only.
80:   - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the
81:     changes, and push again.
82: 
83: ## Pre-commit hooks
84: 
85: To run the checks automatically before each commit:
86: 
87: ```bash
88: uv tool install pre-commit
89: pre-commit install
90: ```
91: 
92: After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` run on staged files whenever you commit.
93: You can also trigger them manually:
94: 
95: ```bash
96: pre-commit run --all-files
97: ```
98: 
99: ## Testing
100: 
101: Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely
102: in-memory — no running server required. Tests live next to the package they
103: cover, and every test runs from the repository root:
104: 
105: ```bash
106: uv run pytest                        # everything
107: uv run pytest apps/cli               # one app
108: uv run pytest packages/core          # one package
109: uv run pytest tests/contract         # cross-package contracts
110: uv run pytest tests/scripts          # dev launcher
111: ```
112: 
113: The MCP server contract test compares the live FastMCP registry with
114: `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py`, so add or change a tool in
115: both places. The CLI local-backend contract test keeps `_LOCAL_HANDLERS` aligned
116: with the same tool names.
117: 
118: ## Test Coverage
119: 
120: CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and uploads one combined
121: `coverage.xml` from the 3.12 job to
122: [Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi).
123: 
124: The Codecov upload authenticates with the `CODECOV_TOKEN` repository secret and
125: is non-blocking (`fail_ci_if_error: false`), so a Codecov outage or a fork PR
126: without secrets cannot fail the test job. The badge at the top of the README
127: tracks `main`, which is the baseline every PR is compared against:
128: 
129: - **Project** status requires at least **90%** coverage (`target: 90%`) and
130:   tolerates a 1% dip from `codecov.yml`.
131: - **Patch** status is informational for now, so new code can land while the
132:   suite catches up.
133: 
134: To reproduce the report locally:
135: 
136: ```bash
137: uv run pytest \
138:   --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
139:   --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
140:   --cov=agentic_odi_core \
141:   --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
142:   --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
143:   --cov-report=term-missing \
144:   --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml
145: ```
146: 
147: > [!NOTE]
148: > Coverage is only collected for the Python packages. `apps/studio/` and test
149: > directories are excluded in `codecov.yml`.
150: 
151: ### Conventions
152: 
153: - Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named
154:   `test_*.py`.
155: - Root `tests/` is reserved for cross-package checks (`contract/` and
156:   `scripts/`).
157: - Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`.
158: - Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests.
159: - The MCP server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before

168: | `apps/studio-api/tests/` | Health, config, canvas, SSE chat, SPA fallback, MCP hydration, probes, and step/outcome passthrough |

# Development

Everything below mirrors what CI runs. Install the workspace first:

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
```

## Linting, Formatting & Type Checks

Shared tooling lives in the root `pyproject.toml`, so one command covers every
Python project:

```bash
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy apps brand packages
uv run --directory website mypy .

# Security scanning
uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages website/
```

## Frontend & Desktop Checks (studio)

The SPA and Tauri shell mirror their CI jobs locally:

```bash
npm --prefix apps/studio run lint       # ESLint
npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run  # Vitest (run once)
npm --prefix apps/studio run build      # production build → apps/studio/dist
cd apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check
```

### Conversational UI coverage

The agent-composed surfaces and the first-run tour are covered at these levels:

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `apps/studio/src/ui/protocol.test.ts` | Spec parsing: prop types, enums, ranges, required props, depth/node/size ceilings, unknown types |
| `apps/studio/src/ui/UiRenderer.test.tsx` | Card rendering, computed opportunity scores, action dispatch, per-node failure isolation, catalog/registry parity |
| `apps/studio/src/components/chat/Conversation.test.tsx` | Prose and surfaces interleaved in the agent's order; card actions become messages |
| `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_ui_spec.py` | Catalog validation and `render_ui` tool-schema generation |
| `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_chat_ui.py` | `render_ui` interception, `ui` SSE events, and the correction fed back to the model |
| `apps/studio/src/features/flags.test.ts` | Flag precedence (query → storage → env → default), value parsing, local overrides |
| `apps/studio/src/onboarding/machine.test.ts` | Tour transitions, no forward motion without a goal, versioned storage, malformed records |
| `apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.test.tsx` | Auto-open, full flow to a destination, skip/Escape, focus trap, resume, replay, inline model repair, flag off |
| `apps/studio/src/App.test.tsx` | First-run ordering: tour over the context conversation, job handoff, chosen surface opens, flag off in shell tests |

## Website Checks (GitHub Pages)

The `website/` static site is part of the main CI workflow. Its tests assert the
committed OG art is reproducible, that `index.html` stays in sync with the
README, and that the publish pipeline (`website/tests/test_pages_deploy.py`)
still exists:

```bash
uv run --directory website pytest tests/
```

Publishing happens in `.github/workflows/pages.yml`: it runs those tests, builds
`_site` from `website/`, and deploys the artifact with `actions/deploy-pages` on
every push to `main`. There is no `gh-pages` branch, so that workflow is the only
thing that keeps <https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/> online.

## Formatting workflow

- **When editing Python files**, either rely on the **pre-commit hooks** below
  (recommended) or run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:

  ```bash
  uv run ruff format .
  ```

- **CI behavior**:
  - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files.
  - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only.
  - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the
    changes, and push again.

## Pre-commit hooks

To run the checks automatically before each commit:

```bash
uv tool install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` run on staged files whenever you commit.
You can also trigger them manually:

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
```

## Testing

Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely
in-memory — no running server required. Tests live next to the package they
cover, and every test runs from the repository root:

```bash
uv run pytest                        # everything
uv run pytest apps/cli               # one app
uv run pytest packages/core          # one package
uv run pytest tests/contract         # cross-package contracts
uv run pytest tests/scripts          # dev launcher
```

The MCP server contract test compares the live FastMCP registry with
`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py`, so add or change a tool in
both places. The CLI local-backend contract test keeps `_LOCAL_HANDLERS` aligned
with the same tool names.

## Test Coverage

CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and uploads one combined
`coverage.xml` from the 3.12 job to
[Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi).

The Codecov upload authenticates with the `CODECOV_TOKEN` repository secret and
is non-blocking (`fail_ci_if_error: false`), so a Codecov outage or a fork PR
without secrets cannot fail the test job. The badge at the top of the README
tracks `main`, which is the baseline every PR is compared against:

- **Project** status requires at least **90%** coverage (`target: 90%`) and
  tolerates a 1% dip from `codecov.yml`.
- **Patch** status is informational for now, so new code can land while the
  suite catches up.

To reproduce the report locally:

```bash
uv run pytest \
  --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
  --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
  --cov=agentic_odi_core \
  --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
  --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
  --cov-report=term-missing \
  --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml
```

> [!NOTE]
> Coverage is only collected for the Python packages. `apps/studio/` and test
> directories are excluded in `codecov.yml`.

### Conventions

- Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named
  `test_*.py`.
- Root `tests/` is reserved for cross-package checks (`contract/` and
  `scripts/`).
- Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`.
- Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests.
- The MCP server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before
  each test.

### Test Coverage Map

| Area | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `packages/core/tests/` | Domain models, opportunity scoring, `ODIService`, repository implementations, SQLite persistence, schema, and repository factory |
| `apps/mcp-server/tests/` | Full ODI workflow, entity parity, context tools, Customer Outcomes, evidence, tool errors, and HTTP transport startup |
| `apps/studio-api/tests/` | Health, config, canvas, SSE chat, SPA fallback, MCP hydration, probes, and step/outcome passthrough |
| `apps/cli/tests/` | Backend selection, local/remote CRUD, chat, wizard, onboarding, updates, rendering, connectors, and startup performance |
| `packages/connectors/tests/` | Catalog presets, registry persistence, factory, MCP and REST connectors, evidence mapping, and sink |
| `tests/contract/` | Live MCP tool surface and CLI local-handler parity |
| `tests/scripts/` | `scripts/dev.py` startup, port checks, signals, and shutdown |
| `apps/studio/src/**/*.test.ts` | SPA units: ODI math, transport bridge, SSE parser, sidecar client |
| `website/tests/` | Static site integrity, OG art reproducibility, and README sync |

> [!TIP]
> Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the
> results automatically.

## Agent Session Tracking

Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview)
CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`,
`.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to
confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured
checkpoints.

"""MCP hydration and passthrough writes, ported from the Streamlit app."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
from typing import Any

from agentic_odi_core import ODIService, ToolName
from agentic_odi_core.remote import (
    StudioError,
    StudioErrorCode,
    parse_tool_result,
    tool_result_text,
)
from fastmcp import Client as McpClient
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError

from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.errors import StudioHTTPError
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.probes import is_endpoint_reachable
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.seed import seed_payload

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT = 3.0


async def fetch_canvas(mcp_url: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fetch live canvas data from FastMCP, falling back to the seed prototype."""
    jobs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    outcomes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    warnings: list[str] = []

    if not is_endpoint_reachable(mcp_url, timeout=0.3):
        log.warning("MCP endpoint unreachable at %s — falling back to seed data", mcp_url)
        return {**seed_payload(), "source": "seed", "warnings": ["MCP endpoint unreachable"]}

    try:
        mcp_client = McpClient(mcp_url)
        async with mcp_client:
            raw_jobs = await asyncio.wait_for(
                mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_JOBS.value, {}), timeout=1.5
            )
            try:
                parsed_jobs = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_jobs))
                if isinstance(parsed_jobs, list):
                    jobs = parsed_jobs
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                log.warning("Failed to parse jobs from MCP: %s", exc)
                jobs = []

            for job in jobs:
                job_id = job.get("id")
                if not job_id:
                    continue

                try:
                    raw_steps = await asyncio.wait_for(
                        mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_JOB_MAP.value, {"job_id": job_id}),
                        timeout=1.0,
                    )
                    parsed_steps = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_steps))
                    if isinstance(parsed_steps, list):
                        steps.extend(parsed_steps)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    msg = f"Failed to fetch steps for job {job_id}: {exc}"
                    log.warning(msg)
                    warnings.append(msg)

                try:
                    raw_outcomes = await asyncio.wait_for(
                        mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_OUTCOMES.value, {"job_id": job_id}),
                        timeout=1.0,
                    )
                    parsed_outcomes = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_outcomes))
                    if isinstance(parsed_outcomes, list):
                        outcomes.extend(parsed_outcomes)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    msg = f"Failed to fetch outcomes for job {job_id}: {exc}"
                    log.warning(msg)
                    warnings.append(msg)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        log.warning("MCP canvas hydration failed entirely: %s", exc)
        warnings.append(f"MCP hydration error: {exc}")

    if not jobs:
        return {**seed_payload(), "source": "seed", "warnings": ["No jobs returned from MCP"]}

    return {
        "jobs": jobs,
        "steps": steps,
        "outcomes": outcomes,
        "source": "mcp",
        "warnings": warnings,
    }


def fetch_local_canvas(service: ODIService) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Read the canvas directly from the local service, no HTTP round trip."""
    jobs = [job.model_dump() for job in service.get_jobs()]
    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    outcomes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for job in jobs:
        job_id = job["id"]
        steps.extend(step.model_dump() for step in service.get_job_map(job_id))
        outcomes.extend(outcome.model_dump() for outcome in service.get_outcomes(job_id))
    return {"jobs": jobs, "steps": steps, "outcomes": outcomes, "source": "local"}


async def call_mcp_tool(mcp_url: str, tool: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Invoke an MCP tool, surfacing failures as typed HTTP errors."""
    if not is_endpoint_reachable(mcp_url, timeout=0.3):
        raise StudioHTTPError(
            StudioError(
                code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
                message=f"MCP server unreachable at {mcp_url}",
                retryable=True,
            )
        )

    try:
        async with McpClient(mcp_url) as mcp_client:
            result = await asyncio.wait_for(
                mcp_client.call_tool(tool, arguments), timeout=MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT
            )
    except StudioHTTPError:
        raise
    except ToolError as exc:
        # The tool ran and refused: that is the tool's failure, not the
        # server's, and it is not worth retrying.
        raise StudioHTTPError(
            StudioError(
                code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_TOOL_FAILED,
                message=f"The {tool} tool failed: {exc}",
                retryable=False,
            )
        ) from exc
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        raise StudioHTTPError(
            StudioError(
                code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
                message=f"Error calling {tool}: {exc}",
                retryable=True,
            )
        ) from exc

    text = tool_result_text(result)
    problem = parse_tool_result(text)
    if problem is not None:
        raise StudioHTTPError(problem)
    return text
